elaine: hitting a weird runtime error when trying to use a server-only helper inside app router on edge. stack says 'module not found: fs' even though I'm not calling fs directly
sam: are you on the edge runtime or node? app router server components default to edge if you set `runtime = 'edge'` in route or layout
elaine: yep edge. the helper is a tiny wrapper that imports `node:crypto`. works in node runtime but fails on edge with a bundler error
ben: edge can't import certain node shims. we ran into this in a sample app — need to either provide an edge-friendly build or proxy the work through a server route
ciara: what's the exact import line? sometimes ESM/CJS interop causes the bundler to pull in the whole Node polyfill tree
elaine: `import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'`
sam: try dynamic import as a workaround: `const { randomBytes } = await import('node:crypto')` - but on edge that might still get bundled and fail
ben: another pattern we used: create a server-only API route (runtime: 'nodejs' / next config) that does the crypto work, then call it from the edge/server component. adds a hop but preserves edge compatibility
ciara: example we landed on — create `app/api/_internal/crypto/route.ts` with runtime nodejs, handler returns hex bytes, then fetch it from edge code. super small and consistent across deployments
elaine: that's what I'm prototyping. question: should DX note or sample app include a tiny proxy helper + type-safe wrapper so users don't have to wire routes themselves? onboarding friction is real here
sam: strongly yes. a recipe in the SDK docs: "Server-only APIs for Node-only modules when using Edge runtimes". show route + client wrapper + typed response

ben: also add retry & auth pattern since the client fetch from edge might need auth headers or retry semantics if you rely on dedicated/private backplane. a tiny SDK helper that does fetch with our auth token + exponential backoff would be nice

ciara: watch out for CORS if customers try this from browser client. but in app router server -> server route it's internal so fine. include example for both server-client boundary and edge -> node fallback

elaine: capturing this: create a sample app PR with two recipes: 1) proxy route for node-only modules, 2) build-time bundling suggestion (vite/webpack externalize node:...)

deploy-bot: Deployed preview for branches/edge-proxy-recipe at https://preview.example.com — tests passing :white_check_mark:

sam: nice. one more gotcha: TS types — if the proxy returns a shape, add zod/schema in the route and export types from the wrapper so client has correct typings. avoids `any` creep
elaine: will add zod + example `type CryptoResp = z.infer<typeof schema>` in wrapper. will draft PR today and ping @devex for review
ben: thanks! also add a short note in the SDK readme about ESM vs CJS consumers — some folks with old bundlers may need `.default` guards when consuming compiled helpers
ciara: ping me once PR is up, I'll test in a tiny Next 14 app using app router + edge functions
elaine: thanks all :thumbsup: will follow up with PR link
